concerns: The headline visual-quality gains are measured with no-reference IQA metrics (MUSIQ, TReS, MANIQA, CLIP-IQA) that are not shown to be calibrated against the curated GPT-Image-2.0 targets or independent human judgments, so the reported superiority over source-resemblance methods is not clearly established.

The downstream corroboration is weak: semantic segmentation mIoU improves only marginally (59.05 vs 58.54 for Text-IF and 58.41 for ControlFusion), and object detection precision actually decreases (94.500 vs 96.414 for MRFS), so the independent task metrics do not consistently support the claimed superior semantic and target representation.

The paper lacks a limitations section and does not discuss hallucination risk, reliance on proprietary LMMs for supervision, small commercial-LMM comparison size, or computational cost, leaving important scientific uncertainties unaddressed.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The paper provides a well-formulated technical method, addresses the classic image fusion limitation of conflicting source-resemblance losses, and corroborates visual findings with rigorous downstream task benchmarks retrained on fused imagery.

ing existing deep methods to indirectly define fusion ob-
jectives by requiring the fused image to simultaneously re-
semble multiple source images. However, the distinct imag-
ing characteristics of different modalities can impose com-
peting constraints on the fused result, potentially limiting
the effective integration of their complementary informa-
tion. To address this long-standing challenge facing the im-
age fusion community, we propose ApexFuse, a novel gen-
erative image fusion paradigm that moves beyond source-
resemblance constraints toward learning a general distri-
bution of high-quality scene representations. Specifically,
we develop a human-LMM-in-the-loop pipeline that lever-
ages large multimodal generative models and iterative hu-
man feedback to translate abstract fusion objectives into re-
liable visual

evidence.excerpt:
ApexFuse aims to turn the long-envisioned ideal of multi-
modal image fusion into a tangible and learnable reality, and
the overall framework is illustrated in Fig. 2. Given a spa-
tially aligned pair of visible and infrared images[Iv, Ir], our
goal is not to make the fused image resemble both sources in
appearance. Instead, we seek to learn a general distribution
of high-quality scene representations while preserving the
factual scene information conveyed by the source images.
To this end, ApexFuse consists of two stages.
Stage 1: We first establish a human-LMM-in-the-loop
pipeline using LMMs and iterative human feedback, as
shown in Fig. 2 (a). This pipeline translates abstract fusion
objectives into reliable visual references, characterizing the
target distribution of high-quality scene representations:

Datasets.We select1,060infrared-visible image pairs
from LLVIP [8], and generate ideal fusion targets using
GPT-Image-2.0. The data are randomly split within each
scene into810training pairs and250testing pairs.
Implementation Details.We employ LoRA for fine-
tuning, with a rankr= 32and scaling factorα= 32.
Training runs for3,000steps using AdamW, with an initial
learning rate of5×10 −5 and weight decay of0.01. During
training, We adopt a cosine learning rate schedule with100
warmup steps and a gradient clipping threshold of1.0. All
experiments are conducted on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
GPUs with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8368Q CPU.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The headline visual-quality gains are measured with no-reference IQA metrics (MUSIQ, TReS, MANIQA, CLIP-IQA) that are not shown to be calibrated against the curated GPT-Image-2.0 targets or independent human judgments, so the reported superiority over source-resemblance methods is not clearly established.

The downstream corroboration is weak: semantic segmentation mIoU improves only marginally (59.05 vs 58.54 for Text-IF and 58.41 for ControlFusion), and object detection precision actually decreases (94.500 vs 96.414 for MRFS), so the independent task metrics do not consistently support the claimed superior semantic and target representation.

The paper lacks a limitations section and does not discuss hallucination risk, reliance on proprietary LMMs for supervision, small commercial-LMM comparison size, or computational cost, leaving important scientific uncertainties unaddressed.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Retrained SegNeXt segmentation and YOLOv8 detection provide task-based measurements, but segmentation gains are marginal and detection precision moves against the headline claim.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: No-reference IQA metrics (MUSIQ, TReS, MANIQA, CLIP-IQA) and downstream segmentation/detection scores.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Curated visual references generated by GPT-Image-2.0 and refined through GPT evaluation plus human selection, used as flow-matching supervision targets.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics and downstream segmentation mIoU and detection mAP scores align well with claims of superior perceptual clarity and effective multimodal integration [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0032, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0037, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0038].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation includes extensive comparisons on visible-infrared datasets against eight baselines using blind image quality assessment metrics, downstream task retraining for semantic segmentation (SegNeXt) and object detection (YOLOv8), commercial LMM comparisons, zero-shot cross-task transfers, and comprehensive ablations [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0032, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0036, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0038, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0040, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0044].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Retrained downstream SegNeXt semantic segmentation on FMB and YOLOv8 object detection on LLVIP provide independent, objective task-performance metrics [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0036, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0038].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard no-reference image quality assessment benchmarks (MUSIQ, TReS, MANIQA, CLIP-IQA) and downstream visual perception tasks (SegNeXt semantic segmentation mIoU and YOLOv8 object detection mAP) [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0032, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0036, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0038].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Target reference images synthesized by GPT-Image-2.0 under multi-step GPT/human iterative curation, fitted via conditional flow matching MSE loss [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0017, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0021, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0028].

primary.limitations: The authors note API-related constraints limiting the scale of commercial LMM comparisons, though broader systematic discussion of hallucination edge cases or computational runtime during inference could be expanded [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0040].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing target curation via prompt generation, GPT-Image-2.0 candidate generation with feedback filtering, human aesthetic selection, token conditioning with 4D positional embeddings, and flow matching loss optimization [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0017, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0020, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0025, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0028].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides a well-formulated technical method, addresses the classic image fusion limitation of conflicting source-resemblance losses, and corroborates visual findings with rigorous downstream task benchmarks retrained on fused imagery.
primary.scoped_contribution: ApexFuse introduces a generative multimodal image fusion paradigm that trains a LoRA-adapted diffusion backbone (FLUX.2) on curated visual targets produced by a human-LMM-in-the-loop pipeline rather than optimizing conventional source-resemblance objectives [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0002, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0016, Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0027].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides a well-formulated technical method, addresses the classic image fusion limitation of conflicting source-resemblance losses, and corroborates visual findings with rigorous downstream task benchmarks retrained on fused imagery.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors note API-related constraints limiting the scale of commercial LMM comparisons, though broader systematic discussion of hallucination edge cases or computational runtime during inference could be expanded [Eaf1a9d20e1b91cc1-B0040].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

relation_to_agentic_memory.value: Segmentation task adjacent to detection; shares backbones and dense-prediction evaluation

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to computer-vision research based on screening evidence.
